causalModel.founding: A gang that works the channel has to sleep on land. The families follow it. The camp is forty years old.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: A slope of firm ground above the marsh, below the Border road. The top terrace stays dry enough for a hatching shed.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: Families whose people are on the roll, living within walking distance of it.
causalModel.pressures: The camp has no claim on the Hist a day upriver. The families stay because the clutch is in the shed.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If the clutch is lost, the families go somewhere the ledger cannot follow.

districts.notes: Terraces of levelled earth cut into the slope between the Border road and the marsh, one shelter on each.

why.what: The gang's camp: two sleeping sheds, two family tents, the overseers' hut and the hatching shed.
why.whyHere: Firm ground within a walk of the barge, below the Border road.
why.whySpot: The slope faces north over the marsh, with the road along its top.
why.whyNeighbours: Alten Corimont is across the water to the north.
why.playerPurpose: Where the gang's families live. The clutch is kept here too.
why.microGeography: A steep slope cut into terraces, each a few paces wide.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door faces north-west, down over the terraces to the camp's fire.

why.what: The hatching shed: a bamboo hut on stilt legs, kept warmer and cleaner than the sleeping sheds.
why.whyHere: The clutch has to be kept dry and warm, so the shed stands on the highest terrace.
why.whySpot: On the top terrace, beside the Border road and furthest from the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The family tents and the cookfire are on the terrace below.
why.playerPurpose: Where the clutch-keeper keeps the camp's eggs.
why.microGeography: A levelled terrace of packed earth, with two lanterns at the door and a totem beside it.

playerPurpose.note: The camp's egg clutch is kept here.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door faces east onto the yard way, in sight of the fire and the sheds.

why.what: The overseers' hut: a bamboo hut on stilt legs for the camp's two overseers.
why.whyHere: The brokers keep their overseers among the families.
why.whySpot: On the middle terrace, between the sleeping sheds and the tents.
why.whyNeighbours: The cookfire is a few paces east. The sleeping sheds are below.
why.playerPurpose: Where the camp's overseers sleep and keep their accounts.
why.microGeography: A levelled terrace with the yard way running past the door.

playerPurpose.note: The broker's overseers live among the families whom they watch.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its open front faces south-east onto the yard way.

why.what: The west sleeping shed: a thatched half pavilion on log posts, open at the front, where most of the families sleep.
why.whyHere: The families sleep under open thatch on the lowest terrace, where the root path climbs down to the reeds.
why.whySpot: On the lowest terrace, nearest the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The second sleeping shed is beside it to the east.
why.playerPurpose: Where most of the gang's families sleep at night.
why.microGeography: Packed earth under thatch, with nets drying at the corner.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its open front faces south, up the yard way.

why.what: The east sleeping shed: the second thatched half pavilion, with the families' cooking things in front of it.
why.whyHere: It stands below the cookfire, so the families who cook sleep closest to it.
why.whySpot: On the lowest terrace, at the foot of the yard way.
why.whyNeighbours: The first sleeping shed is beside it to the west. The cookfire is above it.
why.playerPurpose: Where the gang's families sleep and cook.
why.microGeography: Packed earth under thatch, with a cooking pot and stores in front.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its open front faces west onto the yard.

why.what: The east family tent: hide over poles, on its own small terrace below the road.
why.whyHere: The camp is forty years old, but the families still live in tents and sheds.
why.whySpot: On the east terrace, below the Border road.
why.whyNeighbours: The hatching shed is above it. The cookfire is below it.
why.playerPurpose: Where one of the gang's families lives, with its baskets at the door.
why.microGeography: A small levelled terrace with baskets at the front.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its open front faces north-east onto the yard way.

why.what: The south family tent: hide over poles, a few paces from the hatching shed.
why.whyHere: The clutch-keeper's family pitched beside the shed so that someone is always near the eggs.
why.whySpot: On the south terrace, beside the hatching shed.
why.whyNeighbours: The hatching shed is a few paces to the east.
why.playerPurpose: Where the clutch-keeper's family lives, close to the eggs in the shed.
why.microGeography: A small levelled terrace beside the yard way.

routes.why: The way in from the Border road, to the door of the hatching shed.
The camp's main way, down the terraces from the hatching shed to the sleeping sheds.
A short spur off the yard way to the overseers' door.
A spur across the lowest terrace to the west sleeping shed.
A spur off the yard way across to the east family tent.
A spur off the yard way to the south family tent's mouth.
The end of the gang's walk from the barge, joined to the Border road above the camp.

questSockets.why: The camp's fire on the middle terrace, where the families sit on the night of the raid.
The door of the hatching shed, where the clutch-keeper comes out that night.
The yard way between the overseers' door and the tents.
The dead clutch, inside the hatching shed on the top terrace.
The hatching shed's door, where the clutch is kept.
The yard, read back in the epilogue to show whether the families stayed.

approaches.sequence: The gang's walk from the barge comes up onto the Border road east of the camp. The camp's roofs are below the road to the west.
approaches.wayfinding: Follow the road west, down to the hatching shed.

networkTerminals.why: The gang's walk from the barge ends here, beside the Border road.

combatSpaces.why: Narrow terraces on a steep slope, with drops between them.

candidates.why: The plotted anchor's own slope, on its gentler western side between the Border road and the marsh, where levelled terraces hold every shelter.
The plotted anchor point, at the eastern end of the slope.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The anchor point itself stands on a 16 degree slope, 21 m above the water.
